arxiv-2203-06533.title: A thermodynamically consistent constitutive equation describing polymer disentanglement under flow
arxiv-2203-06533.creator: Benjamin E. Dolata, Peter D. Olmsted
arxiv-2203-06533.description: Abstract We derive a thermodynamically consistent framework for incorporating entanglement dynamics into constitutive equations for flowing polymer melts. We use this to combine the convected constraint release (CCR) dynamics of Ianniruberto-Marriccui into a finitely-extensible version of the Rolie-Poly model, and also include an anisotropic mobility as in the Giesekus model.

arxiv-2210-15696.title: COMET-QE and Active Learning for Low-Resource Machine Translation
arxiv-2210-15696.creator: Everlyn Asiko Chimoto, Bruce A. Bassett
arxiv-2210-15696.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Everlyn Asiko Chimoto, Bruce A. Bassett. Active learning aims to deliver maximum benefit when resources are scarce. We use COMET-QE, a reference-free evaluation metric, to select sentences for low-resource neural machine translation. Using Swahili, Kinyarwanda and Spanish for our experiments, we show that COMET-QE significantly outperforms two variants of Round Trip Translation Likelihood (RTTL) and random sentence selection by up to 5 BLEU points for 20k sentences selected by Active Learning on a 30k baseline.

arxiv-2211-04615.title: Observation of multi-directional energy transfer in a hybrid plasmonic-excitonic nanostructure
arxiv-2211-04615.description: Abstract Hybrid plasmonic devices involve a nanostructured metal supporting localized surface plasmons to amplify light-matter interaction, and a non-plasmonic material to functionalize charge excitations. Application-relevant epitaxial heterostructures, however, give rise to ballistic ultrafast dynamics that challenge the conventional semiclassical understanding of unidirectional nanometal-to-substrate energy transfer.

arxiv-2211-12894.title: An ultra-low field SQUID magnetometer for measuring antiferromagnetic and weakly remanent magnetic materials at low temperatures
arxiv-2211-12894.creator: Michael Paulsen, Julian Lindner, Bastian Klemke, Jörn Beyer, Michael Fechner, Dennis Meier, Klaus Kiefer
arxiv-2211-12894.description: Abstract A novel setup for the measurement of magnetic fields external to certain antiferromagnets and generally weakly remanent magnetic materials is presented. The setup features a highly sensitive Super Conducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID) magnetometer with a magnetic field resolution ∼ \sim 10 fT 10\text{\,}\mathrm{fT} , non-electric thermalization of the sample space for a temperature range of 1.

arxiv-2305-13891.title: Autonomous Control for Orographic Soaring of Fixed-Wing UAVs
arxiv-2305-13891.creator: Tom Suys, Sunyou Hwang, Guido C.H.E. de Croon, Bart D.W. Remes
arxiv-2305-13891.description: Abstract We present a novel controller for fixed-wing UAVs that enables autonomous soaring in an orographic wind field, extending flight endurance. Our method identifies soaring regions and addresses position control challenges by introducing a target gradient line (TGL) on which the UAV achieves an equilibrium soaring position, where sink rate and updraft are balanced.

arxiv-2311-02137.title: Brauer relations, isogenies and parities of ranks
arxiv-2311-02137.creator: Alexandros Konstantinou
arxiv-2311-02137.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexandros Konstantinou. The present paper illustrates the utility of Brauer relations, Galois covers of curves and the theory of regulator constants in the context of studying isogenies between Jacobians and their relevance to the parity conjecture. This framework presents a unified approach, enabling the reconstruction of a diverse array of classical isogenies and the derivation of local expressions for Selmer rank parities, drawing from an extensive body of existing literature.

arxiv-2311-07798.title: Probabilistic Physics-integrated Neural Differentiable Modeling for Isothermal Chemical Vapor Infiltration Process Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2311-07798.creator: Deepak Akhare, Zeping Chen, Richard Gulotty, Tengfei Luo, Jian-Xun Wang
arxiv-2311-07798.description: Abstract Chemical vapor infiltration (CVI) is a widely adopted manufacturing technique used in producing carbon-carbon and carbon-silicon carbide composites. These materials are especially valued in the aerospace and automotive industries for their robust strength and lightweight characteristics. The densification process during CVI critically influences the final performance, quality, and consistency of these composite materials.

arxiv-2402-06440.title: A Method for Decrypting Data Infected with Rhysida Ransomware
arxiv-2402-06440.creator: Giyoon Kim, Soojin Kang, Seungjun Baek, Kimoon Kim, Jongsung Kim
arxiv-2402-06440.description: Abstract Ransomware is malicious software that is a prominent global cybersecurity threat. Typically, ransomware encrypts data on a system, rendering the victim unable to decrypt it without the attacker’s private key. Subsequently, victims often pay a substantial ransom to recover their data, yet some may still incur damage or loss.

arxiv-2509-09340.title: Minimal Help, Maximal Gain: Environmental Assistance Unlocks Encoding Strength
arxiv-2509-09340.creator: Snehasish Roy Chowdhury, Sutapa Saha, Subhendu B. Ghosh, Ranendu Adhikary, Tamal Guha
arxiv-2509-09340.description: Abstract For any quantum transmission line, with smaller output dimension than its input, the number of classical symbols that can be reliably encoded is strictly suboptimal. In other words, if the channel outputs a lesser number of symbols than it intakes, then rest of the symbols eventually leak into the environment, during the transmission.

arxiv-2510-20581.title: Generating pseudo-random unitaries with a Floquet driven chaotic quantum system
arxiv-2510-20581.creator: Alice C. Quillen, Abobakar Sediq Miakhel
arxiv-2510-20581.description: Abstract We explore using an ergodic Floquet quantum system on a torus to generate pseudo-random unitary operators. We choose a regime of the perturbed Harper model with strong perturbations and perturbation frequency exceeding the libration frequency to ensure that the system has an ergodic region that covers phase space and lacks resonant substructure.

arxiv-2512-02590.creator: Kanoy Kumar Das, Rajiv Kumar, Paramhans Kushwaha

arxiv-2604-12816.creator: Katherine Abramski

pmc-10595290.title: Challenges to Implementation of a CHW-led COPD Screening and Referral in rural Uganda
pmc-10595290.creator: R Ingenhoff, N Robertson, B Bodnar, R Kalyesubula, R Munana, F Knauf, T Siddharthan
pmc-10595290.description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks as the third leading cause of global mortality. In rural areas of low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), COPD screening and diagnostic services remain often inaccessible. This study seeks to comprehend the implementation challenges of a Community Health Worker (CHW)-led program for COPD in Nakaseke, rural Uganda.

pmc-10895998.title: Synergistic roles of DYRK1A and GATA1 in trisomy 21 megakaryopoiesis
pmc-10895998.creator: Ying Ting Sit, Kaoru Takasaki, Hyun Hyung An, Yan Xiao, Christian Hurtz, Peter A. Gearhart, Zhe Zhang, Paul Gadue, Deborah L. French, Stella T. Chou
pmc-10895998.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Patients with Down syndrome (DS), or trisomy 21 (T21), are at increased risk of transient abnormal myelopoiesis (TAM) and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (ML-DS). Both TAM and ML-DS require prenatal somatic mutations in GATA1, resulting in the truncated isoform GATA1s. The mechanism by which individual chromosome 21 (HSA21) genes synergize with GATA1s for leukemic transformation is challenging to study, in part due to limited human cell models with wild-type GATA1 (wtGATA1) or GATA1s.

pmc-11325489.title: Anti-inflammatory Lindenane Sesquiterpene Dimers from the Roots of Chloranthus fortunei
pmc-11325489.creator: Xiu-Wen Yin, Jun-Jie Hu, Fu-Cai Ren, Xiang-Dong Pu, Meng-Yu Yang, Bing-Yuan Yang, Peng Wang, Chuan-Pu Shen
pmc-11325489.description: In this study, eight lindenane-type sesquiterpene dimers, including five previously undescribed sesquiterpene dimers (1–5), were isolated from the roots of Chloranthus fortunei, and their structures were elucidated using 1D/2D NMR, HRESIMS, and ECD calculations. Compound 1 presents the second example of a type of novel 8,9-seco lindenane-type sesquiterpene dimer, considered a product of 8/9-diketone oxidation.

pmc-11396586.title: The Cytoprotective Effect of C60 Derivatives in the Self-Microemulsifying Drug Delivery System against Triptolide-Induced Cytotoxicity In Vitro
pmc-11396586.creator: Beihua Xu, Zhenyu Wang, Huimin Zhang, Xiao Xu, Mengjie Tang, Gang Wang, Zhongpeng Ding, Ruihao Yu, Meihong Ding, Ting Zhang, Senlin Shi, Ioana Mirela Vasincu, Lenuta Profire
pmc-11396586.description: Objective: The aim of this study was to optimize the formulation of a C60-modified self-microemulsifying drug delivery system loaded with triptolide (C60-SMEDDS/TP) and evaluate the cytoprotective effect of the C60-SMEDDS/TP on normal human cells. Results: The C60-SMEDDS/TP exhibited rapid emulsification, an optimal particle size distribution of 50 ± 0.19 nm (PDI 0.211 ± 0.

pmc-11467819.title: A Rare Presentation of an Adverse Reaction to Minocycline
pmc-11467819.creator: Francisca Manoel, José Maria Lupi, Isabel V Coelho, Andreia Ferrão, Joana Gaspar
pmc-11467819.description: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) is a rare, severe adverse drug reaction, usually associated with antibiotics and anticonvulsants. A 17-year-old girl with maculopapular rash, arthralgia, fever, and facial edema (plus eosinophilia and hepatitis) repeatedly goes to the emergency department, initially omitting having started minocycline three weeks before symptom onset.

pmc-11618657.title: A viral protein activates the MAPK pathway to promote viral infection by downregulating callose deposition in plants
pmc-11618657.creator: Lixiao Feng, Xiangwen Luo, Liping Huang, Yu Zhang, Fangfang Li, Shijun Li, Zhanhong Zhang, Xiao Yang, Xin Wang, Xian OuYang, Xiaobin Shi, Deyong Zhang, Xiaorong Tao, Jianping Chen, Jian Yang, Songbai Zhang, Yong Liu
pmc-11618657.description: Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are evolutionarily conserved in both plants and animals and play critical roles in activating innate immunity to defend against various pathogens. However, the role of MAPK cascades in positively regulating or enhancing viral infections in plants is unclear.

pmc-11673276.title: Fibrinogen Structural Changes and Their Potential Role in Endometriosis-Related Thrombosis
pmc-11673276.creator: Eleonora Fini, Flavia Rita Argento, Serena Borghi, Elvira Giurranna, Francesca Nencini, Michela Cirillo, Cinzia Fatini, Niccolò Taddei, Maria Elisabetta Coccia, Claudia Fiorillo, Matteo Becatti, Alessandra Napolitano
pmc-11673276.description: Endometriosis (EM), a chronic inflammatory condition predominantly affecting women of reproductive age, has been linked to an elevated risk of thrombosis, though its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this case-control study, involving 71 EM patients and 71 matched controls, we explored the structural and functional changes in fibrinogen and their potential role in thrombosis.

pmc-11960277.title: Prevalence and correlates of meeting the Canadian 24-hour movement guidelines among a sample of Canadian parents during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11960277.creator: Scott Rollo, Abigail Sckrapnick, Julie E Campbell, Sarah A Moore, Guy Faulkner, Mark S Tremblay
pmc-11960277.description: BackgroundParents’ own movement behaviours can influence those of their children, thus contributing to the health and well-being of the whole family. Parents experienced a shift in work and childcare responsibilities during the COVID-19 pandemic. This may have led to a reduction in their healthy movements. This study examined the prevalence and correlates of meeting vs.

pmc-12473992.title: Approaches to Extracting Bioactive Compounds from Bark of Various Plants: A Brief Review
pmc-12473992.creator: Adrian Nisca, Corneliu Tanase, Luigi Milella
pmc-12473992.description: In recent years, focus has been directed toward studying lignocellulosic matter, such as forestry by-products, due to their high therapeutic potential offered by various bioactive compounds, mainly phenolic compounds. To obtain extracts rich in these phytochemicals, suitable extraction methods must be employed, and a thorough understanding of these methods is necessary.

pmc-12529765.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for HIV‑1 Protease Inhibitor Resistance Prediction: Impact of Data Set Construction and Feature Representation
pmc-12529765.creator: Rocío Lucía Beatriz Riveros Maidana, Lucas de Almeida Machado, Ana Carolina Ramos Guimarães
pmc-12529765.description: The rapid emergence of drug resistance in viral infections represents a significant global health challenge, threatening the efficacy of treatments for multiple diseases. Machine learning models have emerged as valuable tools for predicting antiviral drug resistance from genomic data, with HIV-1 protease serving as a well-characterized model system due to its extensive experimental data and clinical relevance.

pmc-12594981.title: Cross-border logistics risk warning system based on federated learning
pmc-12594981.creator: Xinwen Liang
pmc-12594981.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). As international trade grows, managing cross-border logistics becomes more complicated and riskier. This paper aims to build a secure and private risk warning system that allows different logistics partners to collaborate without sharing sensitive information. Traditional systems that try to predict these risks collect all data in one place, creating privacy issues and making it hard for companies and governments in different regions to work together.

pmc-12616098.title: Declining costs make solar plus storage economical for industrial captive power
pmc-12616098.creator: Emilia Chojkiewicz, Nikit Abhyankar, Umed Paliwal, Amol Phadke
pmc-12616098.description: SummarySignificant new coal-fired captive power generation is planned globally to support industrial applications. This is particularly true in Indonesia, where tens of GW of captive coal are in development to support metal processing at least in part for the manufacture of clean technologies such as batteries.

pmc-12718518.title: SIADH and Lung Small Cell Carcinoma: A Clinical Case
pmc-12718518.creator: Nuno Oliveira, Francisco San Martin, Rosa Amorim
pmc-12718518.description: Hyponatremia is the most common electrolyte disorder found in clinical practice. One of the causes is the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH). SIADH is characterized by hypotonic and euvolemic hyponatremia with elevated urinary osmolarity and increased ADH secretion without a triggering stimulus. This pathology is often associated with neoplastic conditions, namely lung neoplasms.

pmc-13133239.title: Effect of copper rod length on the melting behavior of paraffin wax in hemispherical latent heat storage units
pmc-13133239.creator: Abbas Fadhil Khalaf, Farhan Lafta Rashid, Mushtaq K. Abdalrahem, Hayder I. Mohammed, Ephraim Bonah Agyekum, Atef Chibani, Ahcene Keziz, Ali Ismael, Taha Abdel Mohaymen Taha
pmc-13133239.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The inherently low thermal conductivity of phase change materials (PCMs) stills a major limitation for their use in latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES) units, as it significantly reduces the charging procedure and decreases system responsiveness. This study presents a novel numerical examination of the isolated effect of a single vertical copper rod of varying lengths on the melting performance of RT42 paraffin wax within a hemispherical cell.

pmc-13463523.title: A circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network potentially regulates skeletal muscle adaptation to hypoxia in Tibetan sheep
pmc-13463523.creator: Pengfei Zhao, Yaqin Zhang, Jing Ma, Nanjie Dangzi, Wenlu Ma, Xiong Ma
pmc-13463523.description: BackgroundThe extreme environmental conditions of high-altitude regions, particularly hypoxia, pose significant challenges to animal survival. Tibetan sheep serve as an exemplary model for studying mammalian hypoxic adaptation. Skeletal muscle, crucial for movement and energy metabolism, undergoes adaptive restructuring, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms, particularly the role of the competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network, remain poorly understood.
